data.why: The repository ships no raw gel photograph to upload (examples/output contains only already-annotated composite figures, and the built-in example generates a synthetic gel in code via tests/synthetic.py, which cannot be executed here), so stock gel-like images stand in as the upload fixture.

goals: Upload a gel photograph and get the lanes located automatically, correcting the count by hand when a lane ran empty or faint
Label each lane above and below (sample name, genotype, treatment, time point) and add a second annotation tier for a figure panel
Identify which lane carries the molecular-weight standard and have its bands matched to the vendor's stated sizes, with unresolved bands placed from the fitted mobility model
Check the automatically fitted ladder bands against the lot sheet and nudge any marker position by hand before trusting it
Export the annotated gel at 600 dpi TIFF or PDF for journal submission
Script the same load/detect/annotate/save pipeline in Python for a batch of gels rather than through the interface

review.summary: The tree follows the README's workflow closely: load and detect lanes, label in tiers, match the standard and fit mobility, then style and export at 600 dpi. All 11 screens I opened support their nodes, and the known quirks are reported honestly. It needs small fixes before filing: add the crop-to-gel detection step that the README stresses for photographs, correct the label-tier count, and note the Place bands inconsistency the replay found.
